correctness.rationale: For f_C=1_{x>C}, C uniform(0,1), composite trapezoid error equals h B_1({NC}). Splitting a coarse phase into integer fine subdivisions shows Cov(E_i,E_j)=min(h_i,h_j)²/12. Successive coarsening differences are orthogonal, giving the exact sum-of-squares risk for constant-exact coefficients and unique finest-only minimizer. Given the finest-grid sample vector the jump remains uniformly distributed within one cell, and T_finest is its conditional-mean integral, proving optimality among all measurable finite-MSE estimators including independent randomization. The geometric Richardson coefficients follow from Lagrange interpolation at even-power nodes. With q=r^(−2)≤1/4, the signed tails alternate with decreasing absolute coefficients; differences on increasing depth have same initial tail sign and strictly positive magnitude, so every old tail square strictly increases and one new term appears. Uniform q^{j(j+1)/2} domination yields a finite exact infinite-depth limit; for dyadic r=2 the first factors 1,4/3,208/135 and limiting approximation 1.625991555. Independent exact rational finite-depth integration confirms formulas without standing in for all-depth proof.

value.rationale: For an unknown discontinuity, smooth-function Romberg cancellation is an unreliable heuristic. The exact covariance and the strict all-depth relative risk penalty quantify a natural and important failure mode, while the conditional-mean theorem establishes a sharp information baseline. The result is a motivated statistical quadrature classification, not merely a textbook fact about extrapolation coefficients.
